blocks.x: Media economics are attention economics: commissioning, scheduling, promotion and rights all price against predicted engagement. Studios and broadcasters that industrialize audience intelligence and content-operations automation compound catalog value instead of renting it. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in commissioning and audience analysis, content localization/ops, rights/royalty accounting, with ad trafficking close behind. The paths are busy; the decisions are late. Closing that delay is worth more than any single tool purchase.
Media & Entertainment: where the friction concentrates,

items: Linear, streaming, social and box-office data siloed; commissioning decisions anecdotal.
Localization, metadata, trailers and compliance edits consume weeks per title.
Embanked titles leak with catastrophic value loss; supply-chain security thin.
Royalty/rights accounting bilateral; disputes take quarters.
Campaign trafficking and reconciliation by spreadsheet; makegoods costly.

blocks.x: The proof in Media & Entertainment is a working system on a real workflow. These are the builds that go live:

items: watermarking, access control and partner gating
shared rights/royalty records with audited evidence

blocks.x: Privacy (cdpa/gdpr-class) sets the floor for Media & Entertainment: audience data duties. The build adds the evidence layer so compliance is a query, not a project.
